topic: Catastrophe XL - rate on line and payback
t: A cat XL layer of ₹80 crore is bought for a premium of ₹4 crore. The payback period implied by this pricing is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rate on line = 4/80 = 5%; payback period = 1 ÷ rate on line = 20 years, i.e. one full-limit loss is expected to be recouped over 20 years of premium.

t: A single non-marine fire loss of ₹100 crore is suffered by OICL. Under its Risk XL of ₹575 crore xs ₹25 crore, the recovery is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The reinsurer pays the loss above the ₹25 crore deductible: 100 − 25 = ₹75 crore, within the ₹575 crore limit.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: A per-risk XL treaty has a priority of ₹50 lakh and a limit of ₹2 crore. A single loss of ₹1.5 crore occurs. The reinsurer pays
e: The reinsurer pays the loss above the priority up to the limit: 1.5 − 0.5 = ₹1 crore.

t: Where a treaty is terminated for a cause other than the 90 days' notice, the insurer may make termination effective retroactively from
o: the first day of the next financial year
the date of the last bordereau
the inception date of the treaty
the last day of the previous quarter or 31st December of the current or previous year
e: The clause gives the insurer the option of a retroactive termination date as the circumstances warrant.

t: A policy for annual premium ₹12,000 is issued on 1 January. On 31 March the amounts of earned and unearned premium are respectively
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Written premium ₹12,000 is booked at issue; three of twelve months have expired, so earned premium is ₹3,000 and unearned premium (reserve for unexpired risk) is ₹9,000.

t: GNPI for four years: ₹200, ₹220, ₹260 and ₹320 lakh; losses to the XL layer: ₹10, ₹15, ₹8 and ₹17 lakh. The pure burning cost is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Pure burning cost = total losses ÷ total GNPI = 50/1000 = 5%. A loading of 100/70 would give a loaded rate of 7.14%.

t: Under a stop loss cover with retention 85% and limit up to 120%, the actual loss ratio is 110%. The reinsurer bears
e: The reinsurer pays the loss ratio above 85% up to 120%: 110 − 85 = 25%.

t: Retention on a risk is ₹10 lakh and the sum insured is ₹65 lakh. The cession to the surplus treaty amounts to
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Surplus = ₹65 − ₹10 = ₹55 lakh; expressed in lines of ₹10 lakh this is 5.5 lines. Lines need not be whole numbers.

t: A reinsurer provides a Cat XL limit of ₹100 crore for a premium of ₹5 crore. The rate on line is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rate on line = premium ÷ limit of cover = 5 ÷ 100 = 5%; it reduces for each successive higher layer.

t: Under the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, an inward treaty agreement received from a foreign ceding company
o: is exempt from Indian stamp duty
is stamped by the foreign cedant
is stamped only if the premium exceeds ₹1 crore
requires to be stamped in India
e: Inward treaties from foreign cedants must be stamped in India; for outward treaties the copy retained in India is stamped.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: A reinsurer owes the cedant ₹18 lakh towards claims while the cedant owes the reinsurer ₹25 lakh of premium. Under the set-off clause the settlement is
o: the cedant pays the net ₹7 lakh
each party pays the full amount it owes
the reinsurer pays ₹18 lakh and the premium is deferred
no payment until the year-end account
e: The set-off (offset) clause permits each party to net amounts due against those payable before settlement; it is especially valuable if one party becomes insolvent.

t: Retention per event is ₹10 crore and the probable maximum number of risks involved in one event (PMN) is 20. The retention per risk works out to
e: Retention per risk = retention per event ÷ PMN = 10 crore ÷ 20 = ₹50 lakh.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: The obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer was reduced from 20% to 15% in
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Statutory cession: 20% until 2006-07, 15% in 2007-08, 10% from 2008-09, 5% from 2013-14 and 4% from 2022-23.

topic: Catastrophe excess of loss - hours clause
t: A cat XL of ₹60 lakh xs ₹15 lakh per occurrence applies a 72-hours clause to riot within the limits of one city. Rioting in one city continues for five days: losses in the first 72 hours ₹55 lakh and in the remaining 48 hours ₹20 lakh. Recovery is
e: Two occurrences: 55 − 15 = ₹40 lakh and 20 − 15 = ₹5 lakh; total ₹45 lakh, each within the limit.

t: An insurer cedes ₹500 crore of reinsurance premium outside India. The maximum it may place with a single CBR rated 'A' (S&P) is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A rating above BBB+ and up to A+ carries a 15% limit: 15% of ₹500 crore = ₹75 crore.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: Deduction for life insurance premium under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act is available up to an overall limit of:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹1,50,000 aggregate for all 80C items; premium qualifies only up to 10% of the sum assured for policies issued after 1 April 2012.

t: In the cover above (final premium ₹72 lakh) a deposit premium of ₹40 lakh was paid during the year. At adjustment the cedant
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Adjusted premium ₹72 lakh less deposit ₹40 lakh = ₹32 lakh payable to reinsurers.

t: In the same programme (sum insured ₹24 crore; retention ₹40 lakh; 1st surplus 15 lines; 2nd surplus 10 lines; facultative obligatory ₹8 crore), the amount that has to be placed by facultative reinsurance is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Automatic capacity = ₹0.40 + ₹6 + ₹4 + ₹8 crore = ₹18.4 crore. Balance ₹24 − ₹18.4 = ₹5.6 crore must be reinsured facultatively.

topic: Excess of loss premium - maximum rate
t: GNPI ₹6 crore; incurred losses to the XL cover ₹54 lakh; rate 100/70 of burning cost, minimum 5%, maximum 10%. The XL premium chargeable is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Burning cost = 54/600 = 9%; loaded = 9 × 100/70 = 12.86%, which exceeds the maximum. Premium is charged at the maximum 10% of ₹6 crore = ₹60 lakh.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
Both at inception and at claim
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: An insurer with net worth ₹5,000 crore wants to set its retention on a liability (non-property) risk by the thumb rule. The indicative range is
e: Non-property retention is 1-2% of net worth: 1% of ₹5,000 crore = ₹50 crore and 2% = ₹100 crore.

t: GNPI for three years totalled ₹30 crore and losses to the XL cover ₹1.35 crore. Rate is burning cost loaded at 100/75, minimum 5%, maximum 7%. Current GNPI is ₹12 crore. The XL premium is
e: Burning cost = 1.35/30 = 4.5%; loaded = 4.5 × 100/75 = 6%, within the 5%–7% band. Premium = 6% of ₹12 crore = ₹72 lakh.

t: A storm damages five factories. The per-risk XL treaty is ₹25 lakh xs ₹25 lakh with an event limit of three times the per-risk limit. Claims paid are ₹50L, ₹47.5L, ₹30L, ₹42.5L and ₹35L. The total reinsurance recovery is
e: Per-risk recoveries are 25 + 22.5 + 5 + 17.5 + 10 = ₹80 lakh, but the event limit of 3 × 25 = ₹75 lakh caps the recovery.
